title: Remote Collaborative Architectural Review
business: A global architecture firm requiring real-time visual collaboration between field engineers and office-based lead architects.
problem: High-latency video conferencing tools introduce significant lag during complex structural inspections, preventing precise communication and causing costly delays in project approval.
solution: WebRTC enables peer-to-peer media streaming directly between the field engineer's mobile browser and the architect's desktop, bypassing centralized media servers to minimize latency.
steps: Request user permission to access the device camera and microphone using the browser media API.
Initialize an RTCPeerConnection object to manage the connection state and media tracks.
Exchange session descriptions (SDP) via a signaling server to establish the peer-to-peer handshake.
Add local media streams to the connection and handle incoming remote streams for rendering in the UI.
outcome: Architects experience near-instantaneous visual feedback from the field, allowing for accurate, real-time structural assessments without the lag typical of relayed video services.
limitation: WebRTC relies on NAT traversal techniques like ICE candidates to establish connections; if strict corporate firewalls block these, the connection will fail, which can be verified by monitoring the ICE connection state changes.

code.content:
const pc = new RTCPeerConnection(); // Initialize connection
const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({video: true, audio: true}); // Access hardware
stream.getTracks().forEach(track => pc.addTrack(track, stream)); // Add media to peer connection
code.explanation: This code demonstrates the initial steps of accessing hardware and binding media tracks to a peer connection for the Remote Collaborative Architectural Review.
